questions.text: How long did king Ahasuerus shew the riches of his glorious kingdom unto his princes?

options.text: An hundred and fourscore days, and after seven days of feast in court of garden
Forty days in remembrance of the great victory of the Medes against Babylon
Seven full months exclusively for the priests of all the provinces of Persia
Thirty days before the host of the Persians went forth to battle with Greece

questions.text: Why was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him, concerning queen Vashti?

options.text: Because she conspired secretly with rebels against the peace of the realm
Because the queen Vashti refused to come to shew the people and princes her beauty
Because she was sick of body and kept her chamber with the young maidens
Because she wore garments of mourning for the demise of her kindred in Media

questions.text: What counsel gave Memucan before the king and princes concerning the refusal of Vashti?

options.text: That Vashti should be banished one year into the far mountains of Media
That the king should pardon her and make a royal banquet for the women
That Vashti come no more before the king, that wives despise not husbands
That the chamberlains be put to death who brought her answer to the king

questions.text: Out of which tribe of Israel was Mordecai descended in Shushan the palace?

options.text: Out of the tribe of Judah, of the royal seed of king David
Out of the tribe of Levi, of the lineage of Aaron the priest
Out of the tribe of Ephraim, of the household of Joshua
Out of the tribe of Benjamin, a son of Jair, son of Shimei

questions.text: What charge had Mordecai given unto Esther when she was brought into the king's house?

options.text: Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for he had charged her
She should eat freely of the king's meat to appear as one of the heathen
She should demand instant royal homage from all the maidens of the palace
She should send daily letters unto the elders of the captivity at Jerusalem

questions.text: What conspiracy did Mordecai discover while he sat in the king's gate?

options.text: A treacherous rebellion of the governors of Egypt against the crown
Bigthan and Teresh, two chamberlains, sought to lay hand on Ahasuerus
A secret theft of golden treasures from the inner royal treasury
A league of the princes to poison the captains of the guard at night

questions.text: Why did Mordecai bow not, nor did him reverence, when Haman passed by?

options.text: Because Haman had laid a heavy double tribute upon all the Jewish people
Because the king had granted him an imperial letter of royal privilege
Because he had told them that he was a Jew, and bowed not to the Agagite
Because he feared the reproach of the servants that were in king's gate

questions.text: What sum did Haman offer to pay into the king's treasuries to destroy all the Jews?

options.text: Fifty thousand shekels of gold out of the treasuries of provinces
An hundred chosen horses of war with ten brazen chariots of fight
Five thousand oxen and ten thousand sheep for daily royal banquets
Ten thousand talents of silver to bring it into the king's treasuries

questions.explanation: Haman offered to pay ten thousand talents of silver (approx. 340 metric tons) into the king's treasuries [ref:Esther 3:9].

questions.text: Upon what day fell the lot Pur to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish all Jews?

options.text: Upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar
Upon the tenth day of the seventh month at the solemn day of atonement
Upon the first day of the first month Nisan in the beginning of year
Upon the fourteenth day of the month Sivan in the time of the harvest

questions.text: What law was appointed for whosoever came unto the king into the inner court uncalled?

options.text: He was banished for ever into the desolate mountains of Media
There is one law of his to put him to death, except the golden sceptre
He was compelled to pay ten thousand shekels of silver into court
He forfeited all his lands and possessions unto the princes of Persia

questions.text: What faith did Mordecai declare unto Esther if she held her peace at this time?

options.text: If thou holdest thy peace, king Ahasuerus will cast thee out of house
God hath chosen thee because thou art fairer than all maidens of east
Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
The rulers of the captivity have sent letters requiring thy royal help

questions.text: With what resolve did Esther consent to go in unto the king contrary to the law?

options.text: Gather a thousand men of war with spears to attend my steps to court!
I will go in boldly, for my royal crown shall preserve me from death!
If the LORD shew me a token of victory, then will I enter unto him!
Fast ye for me three days; so will I go in: and if I perish, I perish!

questions.text: How did king Ahasuerus receive Esther when she stood in the inner court of the palace?

options.text: The king held out to Esther the golden sceptre, and Esther touched the top
He commanded the guard to lay hands upon her and cast her into ward
He rose up from his throne and set the royal crown upon her forehead
He turned his face away in great wrath refusing to hear any petition

questions.text: What petition did Esther answer when the king asked: What is thy petition?

options.text: That the king would immediately reverse the cruel decree of Haman
Let the king and Haman come unto the banquet that I have prepared
That Haman be bound in chains before the rulers of all the provinces
That Mordecai be clothed in royal apparel and brought into the palace

questions.text: What counsel did Zeresh his wife and all his friends give unto Haman?

options.text: Let him buy out Mordecai with ten thousand pieces of silver from gate
Let him poison Mordecai at the royal breakfast in the king's palace
Let a gallows be made of fifty cubits high, and hang Mordecai thereon
Let him accuse Mordecai before the princes as a spy of the Greeks

questions.text: What came to pass on that night before the second banquet of queen Esther?

options.text: Haman crept secretly into the bedchamber of the king of Persia
A mighty earthquake shook the palace and the gates of Shushan
An angel appeared unto Esther in a dream revealing her deliverance
On that night could not the king sleep, and commanded to bring chronicles

questions.text: What thought Haman in his heart when the king asked: What shall be done unto the man?

options.text: To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?
The king will advance me to be absolute ruler over all Egypt
The king intendeth to bestow upon me the royal crown of Media
Surely this honour is prepared for the high priest of the court

questions.text: What humiliation did king Ahasuerus command Haman to perform without delay?

options.text: He was compelled to pay ten thousand talents of silver to Mordecai
He took the apparel and horse, and brought Mordecai through the street
He was commanded to bow himself down and open the gates of the palace
He was forced to deliver up his private palace unto the seed of Jacob

questions.text: What did queen Esther reveal unto the king at the banquet of wine?

options.text: That Haman was treating secretly with the enemies of Greece
That she had summoned a band of soldiers out of the mountains of Judah
For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish
That the royal treasurer had stolen much silver out of the provinces

questions.text: How answered Esther when king Ahasuerus said: Who is he, that durst presume in heart?

options.text: It is the governors of the provinces beyond the great river!
A cruel captain out of the desolate deserts of Arabia hath done it!
The astrologers of Chaldea have cast the lot upon our households!
The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman!

questions.text: What judgment commanded the king when Harbonah mentioned the gallows of Haman?

options.text: Hang him thereon! So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared
Cast him into the deep pit until he restore ten thousand talents of silver
Banish him for ever into the desolate wilderness of the mountains
Command him to fall down before Mordecai to plead for his guilty life

questions.text: What did king Ahasuerus bestow upon Mordecai following the execution of Haman?

options.text: The crown royal which had aforetime been worn by queen Vashti
His ring, which he had taken from Haman
An imperial garrison of ten thousand horsemen out of the provinces
Absolute rule over all the dominions of Babylon and Media

questions.text: What power did the king's letters grant unto the Jews in every city?

options.text: To withhold all imperial tribute and stamp their own silver coins
To close the gates of all fenced cities against the governors by night
To gather themselves together, to stand for life, to destroy their enemies
To break down every strange temple throughout all the provinces

questions.text: How did many of the people of the land behave themselves after the letters?

options.text: They fled unto the borders of the sea fearing the vengeance of Judah
They confederated secretly with the ten sons of Haman against the city
They petitioned the king to revoke the royal letters of deliverance
Many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell

questions.text: What did the Jews remarkably NOT do when they smote their enemies?

options.text: On the spoil laid they not their hand in any of the provinces
They took no little ones captive to be bondmen in their dwellings
They burned not the dwellings nor castles of their adversaries
They refused to keep the solemn feast of victory in the palace

questions.text: What days did Mordecai establish that they should keep yearly for ever?

options.text: The first and second day of the first month Nisan in the spring
The fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same
The tenth day of the seventh month at the gathering of the vintage
The whole week following the passover feast until the new moon

questions.text: Wherefore called they these days Purim throughout their generations?

options.text: After the Hebrew word signifying deliverance from the captivity
After the Persian name of the royal post that rode upon camels
After the name of Pur, because Haman had cast the lot to consume them
After the royal apparel which queen Esther wore before the king

questions.text: Upon what did king Ahasuerus lay a tribute in the tenth chapter?

options.text: Only upon the cities of the adversaries which were overthrown
Only upon the synagogues of the Jews in the lands of the heathen
Only upon the merchant vessels carrying timber from Tyre and Sidon
The king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles

questions.text: What great advancement had Mordecai the Jew in the Persian empire?

options.text: Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among Jews
He was consecrated high priest over the rebuilt temple in Jerusalem
He reigned as an independent prince over the lands beyond Euphrates
He was appointed chief captain over all the armies in the west

questions.text: What final testimony is recorded concerning Mordecai the Jew at the end of the book?

options.text: He builded high fenced towers round about the cities of the Medes
Seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed
He commanded that the Jews trade no more with the nations round
He gathered all the chronicles of Persia and committed them to fire
